meta.title: Answer the security questionnaire once | nisd2.eu
meta.description: Fill the single supplier security questionnaire once, share with every customer. Structured by ENISA NIS 2 TIG v1.0. Free. Open source.

hero.headline: Answer <u>one</u> security questionnaire.
hero.subhead: One canonical supplier questionnaire, structured by ENISA NIS 2 Technical Implementation Guidance v1.0. Every question names its EU-level source, and customers who manage suppliers under ISO 27001 find the matching controls right next to it. Free. Open source. Your data stays portable.
hero.anchorBadge: Structured by ENISA NIS 2 TIG v1.0 §5

steps.heading: How it works.
steps.lead: Three steps, from first sign-in to first customer invite.

items.title: Create a profile
items.body: Sign in with Google. Enter company name and primary domain. Two minutes.

items.title: Answer the questionnaire
items.body: Three pages in the portal: who you are and what you reach at customers, what you commit to and how you run security, plus questions on software if you offer or ship any. Every supplier answers {always} questions, the rest only where they fit. At your own pace, draft auto-saves.

items.title: Invite customers
items.body: Each invited customer gets a private magic link. No public profile, no search-engine indexing.

sections.heading: What is in the questionnaire.
sections.lead: The questions in the order you answer them in the portal. Each names the provision in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, ENISA's Technical Implementation Guidance, the GDPR or the Cyber Resilience Act that it rests on.
sections.footnote: The full schema is public on GitHub and exportable as JSON.

serviceTypes.heading: What you are asked depends on what you reach at your customers.
serviceTypes.lead: Every supplier answers {always} questions. On your profile you say whether you hold your customers' data, access their systems or enter their premises, and whether you offer software as a service, ship software or run IT for customers. The rest follows from that. A supplier that reaches data, systems or premises also answers on confidentiality, on the suitability of staff with access, and on hand-back at the end of the contract.

items.title: Your customers' data
items.fields: Where the data is processed, the data processing agreement, encryption at rest and in transit. Plus how you manage security: ISMS, certificate, vulnerability handling, plans for incidents and outages, a second factor for your own administrator accounts.

items.title: Your customers' systems
items.fields: Personal accounts with a second factor for every access, remote maintenance included, and a log of access with administrator rights. Plus the same security management as for customer data.

items.title: Your customers' premises
items.fields: How you keep track of keys, badges and codes, and which written rules of conduct your staff follow on site. A supplier that only enters premises is not asked about an ISMS, security testing or administrator accounts.

items.title: Software and managed services
items.fields: If you offer software as a service or ship software: secure development, a published way to report security holes, independent security testing. For SaaS also a second factor for your customers and the time to restore service; for shipped software how long you supply security updates, an SBOM and signed releases. If you run IT for customers, you answer the questions on security testing and security management.

serviceTypes.example: A cleaning company with keys sees {cleaning} questions this way, a SaaS provider that holds customer data {saas}.

preview.heading: Sample questions.
preview.lead: Some questions from different parts of the questionnaire, with the help text suppliers see while filling them in and the provision each rests on.
preview.footnote: {shown} of {total} questions. Full set in the portal.

bsi.quote: We welcome current industry initiatives to develop a unified questionnaire catalogue for suppliers.
bsi.attribution: BSI NIS-2 FAQ (supply chain and security).
bsi.context: This supplier portal is one such initiative: a single, open questionnaire, structured by ENISA TIG §5. Suppliers answer it once, and every customer reads the same answers when it reviews its supply chain under Art. 21(2)(d) NIS 2.

privacy.heading: Bilateral and private.
privacy.body: Built in Germany, hosted in the EU, aligned with BSI Grundschutz. Your data is shared only with customers you explicitly invite. No public URL, no search-engine indexing.

cta.heading: Start in two minutes.
cta.body: Sign in with Google. Enter company name and primary domain. Fill the questionnaire at your own pace. When you are ready, invite your customers.
